§6Tritium§f §aRadioactive hydrogen for fusion, reactor rods, and glowing lamps that make your base look cool.§f §bTritium§f (T, Hydrogen-3) is a flammable, combustible, radioactive gas (NFPA 3/4/0) with high fuel grade. It provides §e5 kTU§f and §e10 kHE§f per bucket. Used primarily in the fusion reactor with deuterium. §6Production§f (§bRBMK Irradiation Channel§f):
§b• Block of Lithium§f → §e10,000 mB§f Tritium
§b• Lithium Powder§f → §e1,000 mB§f Tritium
§b• Tiny Pile of Lithium Powder§f → §e100 mB§f Tritium §6Key Uses§f:
§b• §eMakeshift Energy Core§f, Advanced Alloy + Superconducting Coil + Tungsten + Deuterium + Tritium Cells
§b• §eCustom Nuke Hydrogen Rod§f, Lead Plate + Iron Plate + Tritium Cell
§b• §eTritium Lamps§f, Glass + Red Phosphorus + Tritium Tank + Sulfur → Green Lamp; + Aluminium Powder → Blue Lamp
§b• §eFusion Reactor§f, combined with deuterium for fusion fuel
§b• §eZIRNOX Rods§f, tritium-enriched fuel rods §ePS:§f Lithium is the key input. Set up RBMK irradiation channels with blocks of lithium for bulk production. Each block yields 10,000 mB, enough for 10 tritium cells. The lamps are a nice bonus.
